The other day I got home and the wash room smelled like burnt popcorn. After sniffing around we deduced that it was coming from the washer. A bunch of research and testing hoses and such later, we guessed our water pump motor was likely the culprit. The OEM part was going to cost $50 plus $15 for two day shipping, so I immediately checked Amazon for a cheaper option. I was very suspicious since this was less than a quarter the price, but it would get here the next day and of course free prime shipping. I figured I could return it if it looked cheap or like it wasn’t going to work out.

When it arrived and I got the old one out, I could immediately tell it was the exact same part with the same type of plastic. Of all the things to have to replace on a washer this is one of the cheapest and easiest to install, so when I got it in and hooked up, I was glad the burning smell was gone after the test load.

No idea yet on longevity of this product yet since it’s only been in a day, but so far after a few loads it seems to have fixed the problem. I’m very glad this was the issue and not the motor or transmission. If I had to do it again with the knowledge I have now, I would have just ordered this straight off the bat and had it a day sooner instead of testing a bunch of stuff first.

This is a nifty ice maker but honestly, it is hard to see it being useful outside of some specific niche areas

Size: This is about the size of fat a computer tower, so it takes up some space. It also requires space around it because it has a fan and requires some air circulating around the vents. So you can't snug it in between anything when in use.

Instructions: Need some work. There is a great little numbered list of the functions, buttons, parts of the machine. But there is not accompanying photo to show what the numbers list maps to on the machine. For instance, There are instructions about needing to clean the evaporator rods with vinegar & water before first use, but you have to intuit what those are.

Function: Very easy to use. Just fill the reservoir with water up to the max line, hit the on/off switch, choose what size ice you want (large or small) and go. A little louder than I expected.

Results: It makes ice fairly quickly. For single use, you can get a about 8 pieces of use within about 8-10 minutes. I think it took about an hour to get what would be the equivalent to fill four glasses up with an adequate supply (about 4 cups of water worth of ice and about 1/2 full basket). So if you want to have a large amount available you have to plan ahead. From the Manufacturer:
[Portable design, outsized production] The NewAir countertop ice Maker takes up only about one square foot of counter space, but don't let its size fool you. This compact ice maker makes 33 pounds of ice each day — and looks great doing it. That’s almost the same as purchasing three 10lb bags of store-bought ice in a single day. Choose from three Great colors to match your decor.
[Fast freezing means more ice] need ice quick? The NewAir countertop ice Maker makes a new batch of ice every eight minutes. Use the included scoop and removable ice tray to empty it regularly, and you'll have enough ice for any occasion

I have mixed feelings about this machine. My first beef is with the advertising. The manufactures states "The NewAir countertop ice Maker produces 33 pounds of bullet ice each day, so you'll never run out". While this may be true, it's not at all realistic. You would have to stand near the machine all day and add water and empty out the ice. The bin is quite small and is not a freezer so the ice will melt in short order. It does make a batch of ice in less than 10 minutes, however a batch is about one serving. I'm trying to figure out how this will be useful, but it's just not practical. If you need large amounts of ice for an event, you will be better off purchasing ice and storing it in a cooler. If you need small amounts of ice, I suspect your ice maker could keep up and if you don't have an automatic ice maker in your freeze you could buy plastic ice cube trays for a lot less money. This leaves it for use in a campsite, RV or boat. Again, I think it requires too much attention to be useful and takes up too much space in any of those settings. As far as the unit itself, it's about the footprint of a 6 slice toaster. It makes a batch (small) in less than 10 minutes. About a glass full. The bin holds enough ice for about 4 glasses but is not refrigerated. So in summary, it does make small amounts of ice rather quickly and it's not terribly expensive. However, I think this a novelty item that will wind up as a yard sale item in short order.

When we finished our basement 18 yrs ago, we made a large bar area with sink, small refrigerator (w/ useless plastic ice trays), & tons of counter space...
Why did we not plan for an icemaker?? Can’t remember why such a dumb move, but we’ve been lugging ice down from the kitchen refrigerator the entire time.
Until now.
PERFECT appliance for this use! Basically plug ‘n play after washing the parts that water/ice will touch.
The bullet cubes are excellent - my husband is a vodka on the rocks guy, so ice kinda matters. These have zero smell or taste & melt evenly.
You fill the reservoir with water & 8 mins later, your 1st “batch” of cubes drop. Enough for 1 rocks glass full. They keep making until the bin is full & indicator lights tell you when it’s full or out of water.

We’ve been turning this off when we’re done using it, then back on shortly before needing it again, but if this were for all day use, you’d need to keep an eye on it. If all the ice is made & you don’t use them, they melt back in & make cubes again! Sometimes the cubes stack up to the top & triggers the “ice full” light, so just spreading them out turns the light off & it continues making ice.

There’s supposedly 2 sizes of bullet cubes, but we see no discernible difference. Haven’t put a ruler to ‘em, but they look pretty much the same! No big deal to us - the large is small enough!
The whole thing is about the size of a large air fryer or an old school bread

This is a counter top ice maker. It can make big or little ice tubes, not cubes. It's pretty fast, the first cubes come out in just 5 min or so. It deposits the ice in a little basket that you can take out and dump in your freezer's ice box or where ever you want it.

My only real complaint is that the ice maker doesn't refrigerate the ice after making it. So it's constantly melting. The ice basket has holes in it so the melt water just runs back into the machine, which is nice, but you can't make ice in the morning and have it waiting for you that evening or anything like that. Also if you're using this outside by the pool or something and it's hot, the ice is gone pretty quick. As long as the machine is running it's constantly refreshing the ice but still, it would be nice if it weren't melting all the time.

Other than that, this is a great machine and I would recommend it to anyone.

The ice maker on the refrigerator tends to act up and only make ice when it feels like it. This portable ice maker suits the need when you need it. It won’t store the ice so it is important to know you will have to remove and place in freezer ice bin or ice bucket or whatever else you need to use it for. My daughter entertains often so this machine has saved time by not having to store huge amounts of ice. Makes ice fast (within 10 minutes) so packing the kids lunch boxes has been a breeze. It does have a fan that runs so you would have to have a space that accommodates the flow of air, and it is about as noisy asan older microwave or dishwasher, but we treat it as just temporary white noise.

Perfect for parties!  To love and appreciate this machine you have to understand what it does and what its limitations are. It will make a batch of ice in eight minutes, but that is a small amount, maybe enough for two glasses half filled with ice. And in order to make tons of ice, you have to keep refilling the water reservoir.  So that its limitations. But if you host parties and large family functions it will be a lifesaver. Because you can put it right on your buffet table, and with a little attention to refilling the reservoir, you will have ice all night and not have to run out and buy bags of ice and have a cooler on the side to keep it from melting. Keep in mind that this unit is not a freezer.  The reservoir that holds the ice will not keep it frozen. I can think of it like an ice bucket and use it in that way and a party. I like the fact that it’s foot print is so small. It makes it perfect for party situations and large family dinners. I also like the fact that you have a choice of sizes for the ice, and the smaller bullet sized ice fits nicely in water bottles.  It’s a bit pricey, but I thought it was a good value and invaluable if you do a lot of entertaining.

So I sort of have mixed reviews for this ice maker. It has positives and negatives. First of all, cool gadget. Like that it has two sizes for ice cubes. My girls like the bullet size and shape ice. Much different than the ice our freezer ice maker makes.

It does take up a lot of space for how little ice it makes before it's full. That being said. It makes ice pretty quickly.

Ok, sooooo, this thing is noisy. When it's making ice, or just keeping everything cold it's pretty loud. I was hoping you could make the ice and then stop that option but keep it frozen, but that's NOT an option.

It's either ON making ice, or OFF off. Can't just keep the already made ice frozen in the device without it constantly making ice.

However, it does stop when the tray becomes full, but my experience has been, it melts slightly enough that the ice settles and kicks the maker back into making ice.

The good part is, you just pour water under the basket and that's the water it uses to make the ice. So when you shut it off, it just melts right below the basket and you can use that water again once you want ice again. If you need a lot of ice, you'll have to constantly add water. It is very simple to use.

Basically, it's a neat ice maker, cool if you're having a party and people want ice for drinks. Just need to keep adding water. But it makes ice faster than the freezer.

Received the unit tried it out but nothing?  I tried resetting the unit, power cycling 3 times and it started working.  I ran it for a full load and everything worked flawlessly.  It makes 6 cubes the size of the end of your small finger, fast and efficient.  It loads the ice in the hopper and since the hopper isn't chilled, the bottom ice melts and cycles again.  I found that once the unit senses low water it will shut off.  Filling the water reservoir will not start the machine making ice again, only a power cycle.  So on the initial start up, the machine needed several resets because the lines were empty and it sensed this as a low water condition.  Odd behavior since as ice melts in the hopper you would think the machine would sense adequate water levels and restart automatically.  Gave it a 3 star since it has to be constantly fiddled with.

Incredibly fast at producing 2 sizes of ice cubes, no set up required, takes up less space that a coffee machine on counter top, looks and performs premium, hard to find any reason not to get this if you need one of these and want one that's quality, speed, and efficient, look no further this one is it.

It takes about 45 minutes for the ice maker to complete the cycle. This machine does not keep the ice cold. You will periodically need to scoop ice out of the machine and put it in the freezer. We turn this on when cooking dinner or cleaning up the kitchen.

The machine will beep if you need to empty the ice basket or if the machine runs out of water. We keep the ice in a thick reusable plastic zip lock bag in the freezer.
This ice maker cranks out two sizes of ice cubes: a medium and a small. The sizes are only slightly different.

I have  had this machine for over two months now. I don't usually write reviews, but decided I owed it to the supplier/manufacturer.  Perhaps one of the best purchases I have ever made! We used to constantly run out of ice and had to buy ice from the store.  This machine makes all the ice we need! We use the machine daily.  It takes about 75 minutes for the machine to fill up the ice bucket.  We only use the large ice cube setting. The machine automatically stops when either the ice bucket is full and/or the reservoir is low on water (with red warning lights for both).  The reservoir has clear markings for minimum and maximum water levels.  If we are not quick to empty the full ice bucket, it is not a problem at all since the machine appears to be so well insulated that the ice does not melt. The footprint of the machine is very compact. I figure I will pay for this machine in one year by not having to make trips to the store to buy ice. I hope the machine lasts for many years.  We are so very happy with our purchase!
